about: Single source of truth for conformance case CLASSIFICATION — how a conformance/cases/<name>/ dir maps to a runner, which families carry a non-default validator option, and which families a wasm host skips. Consumers: hosts/conformance-shared/index.ts (both TS hosts, transitively) and hosts/rust/build.rs (parsed at build time via serde_json). The Zig runner (src/conformance_tests.zig) is the REFERENCE and classifies natively — it mirrors this file rather than reading it. Editing a family/marker/precedence here must keep those three consumers in agreement (the classifier audits + build.rs dead-family check are the drift net).

validatorOptionFamilies.label: held-*
validatorOptionFamilies.reason: a document being typed: the case runs with the validator's held_symbol set, so a position spelled `_` is one the author has deliberately not filled in yet. A named option matched by a named prefix, deliberately narrow — there is no general per-case options sibling, and inferring the option from the document would be the document-weakens-its-own-schema hazard arriving through the test suite

wasmHostSkipFamilies.label: lowering-*
wasmHostSkipFamilies.reason: exercises the Zig-side lowering registry + test/identity-v1 hook; a wasm host (web/rust) drives sjon.wasm, which has no Zig-side registry (mirrors the plugin-exec skip shape)

wasmHostSkipFamilies.label: too-many-keys
wasmHostSkipFamilies.reason: validateDocument drops the errored plugin from the schema, so (big …) becomes unknown_form on top of the manifest-phase too_many_keys; the legacy pre-compose path keeps the truncated plugin
